phrases.label: Back when the web was young,
two giants fought to frame the view
for the window we looked through
let more hands inside the frame.
then Firefox stepped into the game.
Add a button, block the track,
and make the browser fit your day.
change the way the pieces play.
More eyes checking all the wiring,
more hands working at the seams.
The doorway had a handle on our side of the screen.
Who decides what you can see?
Let me look, let me change it
Leave the final say with me

browserHistory.title: Netscape source → Mozilla
browserHistory.label: Source released → Mozilla
browserHistory.note: March 31, 1998: Netscape source release; not the Firefox launch. Hardware illustrates eras, not invention dates.

browserHistory.title: Firefox 1.0
browserHistory.label: Firefox · open-source browser
browserHistory.note: Firefox 1.0 released November 9, 2004. Present-day controls are an illustrative openness demonstration, not a reconstruction of the historical UI. Safari/WebKit (2003) is a separate browser/engine distinction; this sequence holds 2004 rather than moving backwards.

browserHistory.title: Chrome beta + Chromium
browserHistory.label: Chrome · built on Chromium
browserHistory.note: Chrome beta and Chromium launched September 2, 2008. Chrome builds on open-source Chromium and adds proprietary components. No lock implies privacy, security, or a wholly closed engine.
